note: 短对话：学生与同学商量去不去职业讲座（en-US-AriaNeural 女声 / en-US-GuyNeural 男声交替，轮次间 0.35 秒静音）

parts.text: Hi Tom, are you coming to the career talk this afternoon?
I was planning to, but I've got a lab report due tomorrow morning.
Can you finish it tonight?
I don't think so. I still have to run the last two experiments, and the lab closes at eight.
Then why not go to the ten o'clock session on Thursday? It's the same speaker.
Good idea. I'll check whether there are still seats, and I'll send you the sign-up link.

note: 长对话：学生向课程顾问咨询暑期田野课程（en-US-AriaNeural 女声 / en-US-GuyNeural 男声交替，轮次间 0.35 秒静音）

parts.text: Good morning, Dr Bennett. I'd like to ask about the summer field course in Scotland.
Morning. Applications closed last Friday, I'm afraid, but we do keep a waiting list.
I only saw the notice yesterday — I was away at my sister's wedding.
That's all right. How many weeks would you like to join for? The course runs for six weeks, but you can come for the last three.
Three weeks would suit me. I'm going home in August.
Fine. One thing to remember: the last three weeks are spent at the coast, so you'll need waterproof clothing.
Noted. What kind of work would I be doing?
Mostly counting seabirds and recording what they eat. You'll work in pairs, and one of the pair has to be able to read a map, because we walk a long way from the road.
I did a map-reading course last year, so that should be fine.
Good. And you'll need to be up before six most mornings, because that is when the birds are active.
Before six? That will take some getting used to.
Everyone says that in the first week. The good news is that the afternoons are free, and the food and the equipment are all included in the course fee.
That's helpful. Is there anything I should do now?
Send me a short email saying why you'd like to join, and I'll put your name on the list. Two students usually drop out before the course starts.
Great — I'll write it this evening. Thank you.
